item.title: Discord Update Adds Correct Markdown Rendering and New Server‑Organization Feature
item.description:
Discord Update Adds Correct Markdown Rendering and New Server‑Organization Feature

Discord released a new update today that fixes Markdown preview rendering and adds a few usability tweaks.

📢 Overview

The company says the update “has a big improvement for Markdown previews: they should now render correctly instead of with “a bunch of symbols,”” and that Markdown files now “render ‘all nice and neat’ thanks to a new update.”

🛠️ New Markdown Rendering

  • “Discord’s latest update released today has a big improvement for Markdown previews: they should now render correctly instead of with “a bunch of symbols,” according to the company.”
  • “Markdown files in Discord now render ‘all nice and neat’ thanks to a new update.”
  • “When you upload a Markdown (.md) file, you’ll now see the file rendered all nice and neat and pretty instead of with a bunch of symbols,” Discord says.”
  • “This includes tables, formatting, all that good stuff.”
  • “Totally great for when you’re doing a casual Sunday-night sharing READMEs with your friends.”
Feature Detail
Markdown preview rendering “now render correctly instead of with a bunch of symbols”
Server/channel organization “new ‘Move to…’ feature accessible by right‑clicking the icon on the sidebar”
Nitro file size limit “upload files as large as 1 GB”

📂 Organization Tools

Discord says its new update also lets you organize servers and channels “by right‑clicking the icon on the sidebar and using a new “Move to…” feature.”

📁 Larger Upload Limits

Discord Nitro members are also now able to “upload files as large as 1GB.”

🤖 Why it matters for AI

“LLMs and AI agents often rely on Markdown files for instructions and context, so these improved previews could be helpful for people sharing information about AI projects on the platform.”

📄 Related Markdown Improvements

Google has also improved its Markdown support, as it recently started “letting users edit Markdown files directly in Docs without having to convert the files to the Docs format.”

#Discord #Markdown #AI #Productivity

Source: Discord now formats Markdown previews right

item.title: Local AI Agent Hermes Enables Personal Automation on High‑Memory Macs
item.description:
Local AI Agent Hermes Enables Personal Automation on High‑Memory Macs

I’m embarking on a journey I’ve so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular, this time by running a self‑hosted agent locally on a powerful Mac.

🔍 Overview

  • Concerns about giving personal data to cloud services motivated a shift to local AI.
  • Apple’s new Mac desktops are marketed for local AI workloads, and upcoming RTX Spark Windows machines promise up to 128 GB RAM for agentic AI.
  • The author’s M5 Ultra Mac Studio has 256 GB unified memory, sufficient for almost any model.

🛠️ How it works

  • Hermes is a self‑hosted AI agent desktop app that runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
  • It is completely free when using local LLMs.
  • The onboarding interface includes a model picker; the author selected Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, a 125‑billion‑parameter model (~105 GB).
  • Hermes can be controlled via a Telegram bot, enabling daily briefings and other tasks.

📦 Devices & Models

Device Memory / Specs Planned Use
M5 Ultra Mac Studio 256 GB unified memory Run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next and other large models
M6 Mac Mini – Try smaller Qwen models
M5 MacBook Air – Try smaller Qwen models
Asus TUF Gaming A14 (AMD Strix Halo) – Try smaller Qwen models
RTX Spark (future) up to 128 GB RAM Agentic AI experiments

✅ Practical Use Cases

  • Daily morning briefing: Hermes scans email and calendar, reports urgent items and weather; set up as a cron job at 7:30 am (macOS must be awake).
  • Steam library organization: After registering a Steam Web API key, Hermes categorized over 400 games in minutes; the key was revoked afterward.
  • Financial record crunching: Hermes processed sensitive financial data locally.
  • Spec‑comparison spreadsheet: Generated a laptop comparison sheet for a new, embargoed device, keeping the information on‑device.
  • Benchmark automation: Working on a script to run repeated laptop benchmark tests, reducing manual effort.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Local AI requires explicit permissions (e.g., Steam API key) that can be revoked after use.
  • Running models locally eliminates token costs; the author chose a large model to start.
  • Larger models (billions of parameters) generally outperform smaller ones.
  • The daily briefing initially failed until the author ensured the Mac was not asleep when the cron job fired.

💡 Why it matters

  • Sensitive data stays on the user’s machine, addressing privacy concerns with cloud services.
  • Free, local execution of powerful LLMs makes advanced AI capabilities accessible without recurring token fees.
  • A single self‑hosted app can automate a range of personal productivity tasks, from email summaries to game library management.

#LocalAI #Hermes #SelfHosted #LLM #Automation

Source: Learning to use local AI is exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating

item.title: Workshop Teaches Building a Competitive Intelligence AI Agent in 3 Hours
item.description:
Workshop Teaches Building a Competitive Intelligence AI Agent in 3 Hours

A new online workshop, “3 Hours to Research Intelligence: Build Your First AI Agent,” lets participants create a custom AI research agent that can save 10+ hours a week on job‑search or competitive‑analysis tasks.

🔍 Overview

  • Current research is fragmented: scattered reviews, Google searches, LinkedIn checks, and missed details.
  • The workshop promises to replace that manual workflow with an automated agent built in just 3 hours.

🛠️ What You’ll Build

  • Fork a ready‑made competitive‑intelligence agent from GitHub.
  • Wire in your own data sources – RSS feeds, open APIs, or any available feed.
  • Feed the agent a company or industry keyword.
  • Receive structured intelligence including recent news, hiring patterns, market positioning, gaps, and red‑flags.
  • Walk away with a deployed agent you can run 100 + times.

⏱️ Workshop Format

  • Duration: 3 hours, online.
  • Pre‑work (optional, 10 min): Clone the repo, set up your API key, verify it runs.
  • Live steps:
    1. Clone the GitHub repository.
    2. Add custom data sources.
    3. Test on a real company or competitor.
    4. Export a post‑work recap doc covering what you built, iteration tips, advanced techniques, and troubleshooting.
  • If you skip the pre‑work, the instructor will set everything up in the first 20 minutes.

🎯 Who It’s For

  • Job seekers who want to research a target employer before applying, interviewing, or accepting an offer.
  • Competitors analysts needing market gaps, hiring trends, and strategic moves.
  • Employees and side‑hustlers looking for a repeatable research workflow.

⚙️ Technical Requirements

  • A laptop with a web browser capable of accessing Claude.ai.
  • Basic comfort with Claude (already asking questions and iterating).
  • Access to RSS feeds or APIs you wish to incorporate.

📊 Modes of Use

Mode Purpose
Job Seeker Mode Research a company before you apply, interview, or accept an offer; understand growth, hiring, leadership, red‑flags.
Competitive Mode Understand what competitors are doing, market gaps, hiring trends, strategic moves.

💰 Pricing

  • One‑time fee of $17–27, covering all materials and the post‑work recap document.
  • Optional upsell: an Advanced Agent Techniques course (separate paid offering).

✅ Outcomes

  • Participants finish the session ready to run their own intelligence agent immediately.
  • The agent can be reused across dozens of companies or industries, delivering consistent, structured insights.

#AIagents #CompetitiveIntelligence #Productivity #CareerDevelopment

Source: 3 Hours to Research Intelligence: Build Your First AI Agent
